newsitem.title: CHINA: China mutual fund closed on profit disappointment.
newsitem.headline: China mutual fund closed on profit disappointment.

text.p: A Chinese mutual fund has been wound up by its operator and its assets returned to investors because it failed to reach expected profit levels, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.

The paper said this was the first case of a local Chinese mutual fund being wound up since they were first established in the early 1990s as a vehicle for investment in the stock markets and property.
The unnamed fund, with assets of 120 million yuan, was set up by the Anhui Trust & Invest Co in 1992 and subsequently issued annual dividends of between 10 and 20 percent.
The paper gave no further explanation of the case.
Many mutual funds in China were started and sold to investors on the expectation that they would quickly obtain the right to list on the stock market.
But most of the funds have failed to obtain approval to list, leaving many investors stuck with units that they can't sell.
There are about 70 mutual funds in China, with assets totalling 10 billion yuan ($1.2 billion), but only 22 are listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges.
